hook.text: You tried on 40 pairs of jeans to find the perfect fit. Your friend grabbed the first good pair and left happy.

buildup.text: Maximizers search for the best possible option. Satisficers pick the first option that meets their threshold.

discovery.text: Herbert Simon coined satisficing—a blend of satisfy and suffice. It's how bounded rationality actually works.

twist.text: Research shows maximizers often get objectively better outcomes but feel worse about them. More choice, more regret.

climax.text: When stakes are low, satisfice. When stakes are high, maximize—but set a stopping rule first.

punchline.text: Good enough is often the best choice.

quiz.question: What is satisficing?
options: Choosing the first option that meets a minimum threshold
